label: Bible Study
prompt: This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt _____ therein day and night, that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success.
verse: This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night, that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success.
note: Joshua's marching orders after Moses died — success, it turns out, starts with a book.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: I will not leave you _____: I will come to you.
verse: I will not leave you comfortless: I will come to you.
note: The night before the cross Jesus promises not to leave them comfortless — modern versions say 'as orphans.'

label: Sunday School
prompt: And when she could not longer hide him, she took for him an ark of _____, and daubed it with slime and with pitch, and put the child therein; and she laid it in the flags by the river's brink.
verse: And when she could not longer hide him, she took for him an ark of bulrushes, and daubed it with slime and with pitch, and put the child therein; and she laid it in the flags by the river's brink.
note: Baby Moses' basket is an 'ark' in the KJV, tucked among the bulrushes at the river's edge.

label: Deep Water
prompt: Behold, all souls are mine; as the soul of the father, so also the soul of the son is mine: the soul that _____, it shall die.
verse: Behold, all souls are mine; as the soul of the father, so also the soul of the son is mine: the soul that sinneth, it shall die.
note: The exiles blamed their fathers' sins; Ezekiel retired the sour-grapes proverb — each soul answers for itself.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: And Jesus said unto him, No man, having put his hand to the _____, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God.
verse: And Jesus said unto him, No man, having put his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God.
note: Look back while plowing and the furrow goes crooked. The KJV spells it the British way: 'plough.'
